title: Embedding volume slab experiment + enterprise QSA playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Objective: validate a multi-tier per-vector pricing slab plus explicit batch-discount that preserves revenue while lowering effective unit price for large-volume reranking customers. This ticket covers the experiment design, canonical pricing table proposals, downstream contract language for QSA/security review, and a short playbook for sales/CS to operate the pilot.

Context: Large enterprise customers running reranking pipelines are sensitive to per-vector economics. Current per-vector proposals reduce friction but risk revenue leakage if we over-discount for high-volume synchronous rerank workloads. We need a pricing construct that: (1) offers a predictable volume discount for customers with steady throughput, (2) provides a batch-discount multiplier when customers submit vectors in grouped calls (bulk/async), and (3) maps cleanly into enterprise contract language and QSA expectations for metering and auditability.

Scope: define slabs (e.g., 0-1M, 1M-10M, 10M-100M vectors/month), batch multipliers for synchronous vs asynchronous ingestion, simulate revenue impacts on top-10 customers, author QSA checklist for how usage is logged/attested, and prepare PRD + sales playbook for a 12-week pilot with 3 customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pricing table with concrete unit prices and batch multipliers approved by finance and revenue ops. 2) Simulation workbook showing expected revenue delta for top-10 customers under three traffic profiles (steady, spiky, seasonal). 3) QSA playbook draft that outlines logging, metering endpoints, and audit artifacts for inclusion in contracts. 4) Pilot onboarding checklist and 3 identified pilot customers committed. 5) A/B experiment flags defined for safe rollback and telemetry instrumentation planned.
